(BY SRI M.K. SOUDAGR, ADVOCATE FOR R1 AND R2)
 THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER  SECTION 173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT 1988, AGAINST THE  JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 11.04.2019 PASSED IN MVC  NO.140/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND  SESSIONS JUDGE AT GADAG, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM  PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF Smt.Laxmavva W/O Ningappa Hittalamani vs Managing Director And Self-Insurance on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99321753/
1  COMPENSATION AND ETC.,
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,

S G PANDIT, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7937-DB  MFA No. 103527 of 2019  JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with consent of both sides, it is taken up for disposal.

2. The claimants are before this Court in this appeal, dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by learned Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Gadag (for short 'Tribunal') dated 11.04.2019 in M.V.C. No. 140/2017.

3. Heard Sri Siddappa Sajjan for Sri G.S.Hulmani, learned counsel for the appellants and Sri M.K.
Soudagar, learned counsel for respondents.
Perused the appeal papers.

4. Brief facts of the case are that the claimants, mother and brother of one Manjappa Hittalamani,
filed claim petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the accidental death of Manjappa Hittalamani, in a road traffic accident that took place on 13.03.2017 involving KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No. KA-09-F-4912.
It is stated that the deceased was working as Poura Karmika and was earning more than Rs.25,000/- per month as salary.
Deceased was aged 42 years as on the date of accident and he was unmarried.
On service of notice, respondents-Corporation appeared before the Tribunal and not filed statement of objections.
6. On behalf of the claimants, mother of the deceased examined herself as PW1 and another person was examined as PW2.
Documents at Exs.P.1 to P.13 were marked.
No evidence was let in by the respondents.

7. The Tribunal based on the materials on record awarded total compensation of Rs.10,95,096/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

While awarding the compensation, the Tribunal assessed monthly income of the deceased at Rs.15,172/-, added 30% of the same towards future prospects, deducted 50% towards personal expenses of the deceased since he was unmarried, adopted multiplier of 9 taking the age of the mother.
8. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants would submit that the Tribunal has committed a grave error in adopting the multiplier of '9' taking the age of the mother of the deceased.

He would Smt.Laxmavva W/O Ningappa Hittalamani vs Managing Director And Self-Insurance on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99321753/
2 further submit that it is the settled position of law that while determining compensation on the head of loss of dependency, age of the deceased shall have to NC: 2024:KHC-D:7937-DB be taken and not the age of the mother.

sentences.text: As the age of deceased was 42 years, learned counsel would pray for adopting multiplier '14'.

Learned counsel would submit that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is not in consonance with the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others1.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus he prays for allowing the appeal.
9. Learned counsel Sri M.K.Soudagar, appearing for the Corporation would submit that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just compensation which needs no interference.
He would further submit that income of the deceased was determined taking note of Ex.P.10-salary certificate.
Further, learned counsel would not dispute the settled position of law that while determining compensation, age of the deceased shall have to be taken.
Thus he prays for passing appropriate judgment.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers the only point which arises for our consideration is as to:
AIR 2017 SC 5157 NC: 2024:KHC-D:7937-DB "While determining compensation on the head of loss of dependency, whether the Tribunal is justified in adopting the multiplier of '9' taking the age of the mother of the deceased?"
12.
Our answer to the above point is 'partly in the negative' for the following reasons.
13. The accident which took place on 13.03.2017 involving the KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No. KA-09-F-4912 and the resultant death of Manjappa Hittalamani, is not in dispute in this appeal.
The respondents have not filed any appeal and it has satisfied the award.
14. Admittedly, the deceased was 42 years as on the date of accident.
It is the settled position of law that for determination of compensation, age of the deceased shall have to be taken and not the age of the mother of the deceased.
Therefore, adopting the multiplier of '9' taking the age of the mother of the deceased is wholly erroneous and opposed to settled position of law.

Thus, taking note of the age of the deceased at 42 years, the proper and appropriate multiplier would be '14'.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7937-DB 15.
The Tribunal has rightly applied future prospects at 30% of the assessed income of the deceased.

Thus, the claimant no.1 is entitled for a sum of Rs.16,56,816/-
(Rs.15,172/- +30% = 19,724/- less 50% = Rs.9,862/-x12x14)
16.
The Tribunal also did not award compensation under the head of 'consortium'.
Claimant no.1 is the mother and claimant no.2 is the brother of the deceased.
They are entitled for a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards consortium.
